tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Free; reads only. Finds the TollNode tools for a task and returns each match's name, title, one-line purpose, category and price per call, best matches first. Use it first whenever you need a capability (make an image or video, a voice or song, read a web page, search Google or Maps, get LinkedIn, Y

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: Free; reads only. Returns everything needed to run one tool: what it does, when to use it and when not, its full JSON input schema with limits, its price per call and price options, its actions (for platform tools such as linkedin or google), an example input and its web page. Call it after search_t

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description: Runs one TollNode tool and returns its result: text, data, or links to the files it made. Spends money: the tool's price (see get_tool) is charged only when the call returns a usable result; a refused input, a failure or an empty result costs nothing. Every successful call is charged again, so do no

tools.name: get_call
tools.description: Free; reads only. Looks up one of your earlier account calls by its request id (given after every charged run_tool result and in errors): whether it is running, succeeded, failed or was rejected, what it was charged, the error code and message if it failed, the API key that made it, and its result a

tools.name: list_calls
tools.description: Free; reads only. Lists your recent account calls, newest first: the tool, whether it succeeded, failed, was rejected (refused before running) or is still running, what it was charged (failed and rejected calls cost $0), the error code and message of a failed or rejected call, the name of the API ke

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Free. A tool request is capped at 4.5 MB in total, and inline base64 files count toward it (base64 adds a third). For a bigger file, or any local file you would rather not inline (a long voice track, a full-size photo, a video), call this first: it returns a one-time uploadUrl and the fileUrl the fi

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Free; reads only. Returns your prepaid account balance in US dollars, so you can check a batch is affordable before running it. Needs an account API key on the connection (Authorization: Bearer tn_live_…). With x402 there is no balance: each call is paid from your own wallet.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_balance" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Free; reads only. Returns your prepaid account balance in US dollars, so you can check a batch is affordable before running it. Needs an account API key on the …

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_tools, get_tool, get_call, list_calls · Private data: run_tool, get_call, list_calls, upload_file, get_balance · Public sink: run_tool, upload_file · Destructive: get_tool, run_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_tools, get_tool, get_call, list_calls · Private data: run_tool, get_call, list_calls, upload_file, get_balance · Public sink: run_tool, upload_file · Destructive: get_tool, run_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
